/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Temporal
  The temporal operators over a whole trace at once: every operator maps per-instant arrays to a
  per-instant array in one pass (or one pass plus O(1) window queries), so a formula costs
  O(|φ| · n log n) per grounding. Semantics and Derived both use these; nothing here knows what
  a formula or a road user is.

  Finite-trace policy: the unobserved past and future are unknown (`windowTruncated`), never a
  verdict. A lookback window must be covered and adequately sampled; a lookahead window is true
  on a witness, false only when covered.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Time
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Temporal

def const (n : Nat) (r : R) : Array R := Array.replicate n r
def truncated (op : String) : R := R.u (.windowTruncated op)

-- pointwise connectives
def zipAnd (a b : Array R) : Array R := Array.zipWith R.and a b
def zipOr (a b : Array R) : Array R := Array.zipWith R.or a b
def zipImplies (a b : Array R) : Array R := Array.zipWith R.implies a b
def mapNot (a : Array R) : Array R := a.map R.not
def allOf (n : Nat) (xs : List (Array R)) : Array R := xs.foldl zipAnd (const n R.t)
def anyOf (n : Nat) (xs : List (Array R)) : Array R := xs.foldl zipOr (const n R.f)

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Unbounded operators: one backward or forward pass with the unobserved tail as unknown.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
private def backward (tail : R) (step : R → R → R) (vals : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := vals.size
  ((List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := step vals[i]! acc.2
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n tail, tail)).1

private def forward (head : R) (step : R → R → R) (vals : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := vals.size
  ((List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := step vals[i]! acc.2
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n head, head)).1

/-- `always φ`: φ here and at every later observation, and the unobserved future. -/
def alwaysAll (φ : Array R) : Array R := backward (truncated "always") R.and φ
/-- `eventually φ`: φ here or later, or the unobserved future. -/
def eventuallyAll (φ : Array R) : Array R := backward (truncated "eventually") R.or φ
/-- Strong until: `ψ ∨ (φ ∧ until')`, the unobserved future as the tail. -/
def untilAll (φ ψ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := ψ.size
  ((List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := R.or ψ[i]! (R.and φ[i]! acc.2)
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n (truncated "until"), truncated "until")).1
/-- Since: `ψ ∨ (φ ∧ since')`, the unobserved past as the head. -/
def sinceAll (φ ψ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let n := ψ.size
  ((List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array R × R) i =>
    let r := R.or ψ[i]! (R.and φ[i]! acc.2)
    (acc.1.set! i r, r)) (Array.replicate n (truncated "since"), truncated "since")).1
/-- `once φ`: φ here or at some earlier observation, or the unobserved past. -/
def onceAll (φ : Array R) : Array R := forward (truncated "once") (fun v acc => R.or v acc) φ
/-- φ at the previous observation (`first` at the trace start). -/
def prevAll (first : R) (φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i => if i = 0 then first else φ[i - 1]!

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Metric windows: positions per instant (time or path), a length d, per-instant values.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- φ at every observation in the window of length `d` behind each instant. Unknown where a
    position inside the window is missing; where the window is not covered, false on a false
    already observed inside it and unknown otherwise; unknown where it is covered but not
    adequately sampled. -/
def holdsForAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.backWindows pos d
  let agg := RangeAgg.build φ
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>
      if !w.covered then (if (agg.all w.j0 i).v = .f then R.f else truncated op)
      else if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op)
      else agg.all w.j0 i

/-- The value of φ at the latest observation `j` in `[j0, i]` at which ψ held: unknown where ψ is
    unknown at an observation later than any at which it held; none where ψ held nowhere in the range. -/
private def atLastAt (ψ φ : Array R) (j0 i : Nat) : Option R :=
  (List.range (i + 1 - j0)).foldl (fun (acc : Option R) k =>
    match acc with
    | some r => some r
    | none =>
      let j := i - k
      match ψ[j]!.v with
      | .t => some φ[j]!
      | .u => some ⟨.u, ψ[j]!.why⟩
      | .f => none) none

/-- φ at the last observation in the window of length `d` behind each instant at which ψ held.
    Unknown where a position is missing, where ψ is unknown later than any observation at which it
    held, where the window is not adequately sampled (an unobserved later instant could be the last
    one at which ψ held), and where ψ held nowhere in a window that is not covered; false where ψ
    held nowhere in a covered, adequately sampled window. -/
def atLastAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (ψ φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.backWindows pos d
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>
      match atLastAt ψ φ w.j0 i with
      | some r => if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op) else r
      | none => if !w.covered then truncated op else if !w.adequate then R.u (.samplingGap op) else R.f

/-- φ at some observation in the window of length `d` ahead: true on a witness, false only when
    the window is covered, unknown when it runs off the trace. -/
def withinAll (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) (op : String) (missing : UnknownReason) (φ : Array R) : Array R :=
  let wins := Time.forwardWindows pos d
  let agg := RangeAgg.build φ
  (Array.range φ.size).map fun i =>
    match wins[i]! with
    | none => R.u missing
    | some w =>

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions
  Declared intentions: what a source declares a road user intends at a target region.

  No camera sees an intention. It reaches a rule through this one door, three-valued and per
  scene: the source's declaration current at that scene, for one road user at one target region,
  true or false per id, or absent where the declaration does not decide the id or the source has
  no current plan for the pair. The ids are `int.*` strings declared by the plan per node and
  recorded by the harness; nothing enumerates them here.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.World

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- Well-formed intention id: `int.` followed by a snake-case name. -/
def IntId.wellFormed (id : IntId) : Bool :=
  let rest := (id.drop 4).toString
  id.startsWith "int." && !rest.isEmpty && rest.all (fun c => c.isLower || c.isDigit || c == '_')

/-- The declared value of `id` for road user `x` at region `r` at this scene, or `none` where the
    pair or the id is not declared. -/
def Scene.intention (s : Scene) (id : IntId) (x : TrackId) (r : RegionId) : Option Bool :=
  (s.intents.find? fun d => d.vehicle == x && d.target == r).bind fun d => (d.values.find? (·.1 == id)).map (·.2)

/-- A relation a source supplies measured rather than derived; `visible` is only ever supplied. -/
structure MeasuredRelation where
  a : TrackId
  b : TrackId
  centreDistance : Option Q := none
  surfaceGap : Option (Q × Q) := none        -- nearest-point gap along, across a's heading; ≥ 0
  aAheadOfB : Option Bool := none
  longitudinalOverlap : Option Q := none     -- shared length of the projections on a's heading
  oncoming : Option Bool := none
  sameDirection : Option Bool := none
  bearing : Option Vec := none               -- b relative to a, in a's frame (long, lat)
  contact : Option Bool := none
  visible : Option Bool := none              -- b in a's line of sight
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A source's declaration current at a scene for one road user at one target region: each id
    listed true or false, an id the declaration does not decide left out. -/
structure DeclaredIntent where
  vehicle : TrackId
  target : RegionId
  values : List (IntId × Bool)
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure Scene where
  t : Timestamp
  subject : Option TrackId := none
  users : List RoadUser := []
  structures : List Structure := []
  devices : List Device := []
  /-- The tracks whose occupancy was observed: for them every region not listed in `occupies` is
      not occupied; for any other track `rel.occupies` is unknown. -/
  occupancyObserved : List TrackId := []
  occupies : List (TrackId × RegionId) := []
  relations : List MeasuredRelation := []
  env : Env := {}
  assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []
  intents : List DeclaredIntent := []
  links : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A trace: scenes in strictly increasing time. -/
abbrev Trace := List Scene

namespace Scene
def user (s : Scene) (x : TrackId) : Option RoadUser := s.users.find? (·.track == x)
def structure? (s : Scene) (r : RegionId) : Option Structure := s.structures.find? (·.id == r)
def device (s : Scene) (d : DeviceId) : Option Device := s.devices.find? (·.id == d)
def relation (s : Scene) (a b : TrackId) : Option MeasuredRelation :=
  s.relations.find? (fun m => m.a == a && m.b == b)
def tracks (s : Scene) : List TrackId := s.users.map (·.track)
end Scene

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Projections a trace check reads, so that it names no field of these records itself. A field a
-- split may omit is named on a line of its own.
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- A reference a scene makes to an entity: where it is written, the kind of entity it names, the
    id, and the structure kinds of which that entity must have one (by refinement) when the field
    requires one. -/
structure Reference where
  place : String
  kind : EntityKind
  id : Nat
  structureKinds : List StructureKind := []
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace Structure
/-- The regions a structure's own fields name: its lane's neighbours, successors and intersection,
    the ways it lies on, and the carriers whose entrance it marks. -/
def references (st : Structure) : List Reference :=
  let at_ := fun (f : String) => s!"structure {st.id} {f}"
  (st.lane.bind (·.leftNeighbour)).toList.map (fun r => { place := at_ "lane.left", kind := .region, id := r })
  ++ (st.lane.bind (·.rightNeighbour)).toList.map (fun r => { place := at_ "lane.right", kind := .region, id := r })
  ++ ((st.lane.bind (·.leadsTo)).getD []).map (fun r => { place := at_ "lane.leads_to", kind := .region, id := r })
  ++ (st.lane.bind (·.entersIntersection)).toList.map (fun r => { place := at_ "lane.enters_intersection", kind := .region, id := r })
  ++ (st.ways.getD []).map (fun r => { place := at_ "ways", kind := .region, id := r })

/-- Quantified variables: the intersection, the subject's entry carrier, the other road user and its carrier. -/
def vX : Arg := .var "X"
def vC1 : Arg := .var "c1"
def vV : Arg := .var "v"
def vC2 : Arg := .var "c2"

/-- a, f: membership of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. -/
def isVehicle (a : Arg) : Formula := .atom "ru_aggregate" [a, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []

/-- rel.occupies: the road user's footprint overlaps the region. -/
def occupies (a r : Arg) : Formula := .atom "rel_occupies" [a, r] []

/-- st.lane_enters: carrier `c` is an approach to intersection `x`. -/
def enters (c x : Arg) : Formula := .atom "st_lane_enters" [c, x] []

/-- st.lane_direction component of a carrier (normalised as Core reads it). -/
def dirComp (c : Arg) (k : String) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [c, .lit k]

/-- f: the designated directions of c1 and c2 are opposed: their dot product is below −p.oncoming_heading_cos. -/
def opposedCarriers : Formula :=
  .cmp (.add (.mul (dirComp vC1 "x") (dirComp vC2 "x")) (.mul (dirComp vC1 "y") (dirComp vC2 "y")))
    .lt (.neg pOncomingHeadingCos)

/-- e, h: danger of a crash / immediate hazard — the centres of subject and v approach within
    p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. -/
def conflict : Formula :=
  .and (.derived "prim_closest_approach_within" [vSubject, vV] [pConflictHorizon])
       (.cmp (.quantity "prim_closest_approach_distance" [vSubject, vV] [pConflictHorizon]) .lt pConflictCentreClearance)

/-- e: the subject proceeds — kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. -/
def proceeds : Formula := .cmp (.measure "kin_speed" [vSubject]) .gt pHaltSpeedTolerance

/-- b, c: the subject's footprint overlaps intersection X and it declares int.left_turn at X. -/
def selectsX : Formula :=
  .and (occupies vSubject vX) (.intent "int.left_turn" vSubject vX)

/-- c1: a carrier (not X itself) entering X that the subject occupied when it last entered X:
    it has overlapped X continuously since an observation at which it occupied c1. -/
def entryCarrier : Formula :=
  .and (.not (.same vC1 vX))
    (.and (enters vC1 vX) (.since (occupies vSubject vX) (occupies vSubject vC1)))

/-- f, g, h: v is another vehicle approaching from the opposite direction — on a carrier c2 (not X
    itself) entering X, or in X continuously since it occupied such a c2, c2's direction opposed to
    c1's — and v either overlaps X or, on c2, is in conflict with the subject. -/
def opposingVehicle : Formula :=
  .and (isVehicle vV)
    (.and (.not (.same vV vSubject))
      (.existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c2"
        (.and (.not (.same vC2 vX))
          (.and (enters vC2 vX)
            (.and (.since (occupies vV vX) (occupies vV vC2))
              (.and opposedCarriers
                (.or (occupies vV vX) (.and (occupies vV vC2) conflict))))))))

/-- d, e: yield — no contact with v, and not proceeding while in conflict with v. -/
def yields : Formula :=
  .and (.not (.atom "rel_contact" [vSubject, vV] []))
       (.not (.and proceeds conflict))

/-- Class of `subject`: ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle -/
def clsSubject : Formula := isVehicle vSubject

/-- Applicability: b (trigger): within an intersection; c (trigger): intending to turn to the left.
    The conditions f, g select the protected vehicles inside the obligation, as the record states. -/
def applicability : Formula := .existsRegion (.lit "intersection") "X" selectsX

/-- Obligation: d (obligation): shall yield; e (standard): the right-of-way; h (standard): or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .forallRegion (.lit "intersection") "X"
    (.implies selectsX
      (.forallRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c1"
        (.implies entryCarrier
          (.forallUser "v" (.implies opposingVehicle yields)))))

import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule

namespace TrafficSpec.Rules.NRS_484B_253_o1

/-- The binders, as arguments (order and names are the node's). -/
def vSubject : Arg := .var "subject"

/-- The reading's parameters; no value of any of them lives in this file. -/
def pConflictCentreClearance : Term := .param "p.conflict_centre_clearance"
def pConflictHorizon : Term := .param "p.conflict_horizon"
def pHaltSpeedTolerance : Term := .param "p.halt_speed_tolerance"
def pOncomingHeadingCos : Term := .param "p.oncoming_heading_cos"

def zeroMetres : Term := .lit Q.zero .metre

/-- Quantified variables: the intersection, the subject's entry carrier, the other road user and its carrier. -/
def vX : Arg := .var "X"
def vC1 : Arg := .var "c1"
def vV : Arg := .var "v"
def vC2 : Arg := .var "c2"

/-- a, f: membership of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. -/
def isVehicle (a : Arg) : Formula := .atom "ru_aggregate" [a, .lit "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"] []

/-- rel.occupies: the road user's footprint overlaps the region. -/
def occupies (a r : Arg) : Formula := .atom "rel_occupies" [a, r] []

/-- st.lane_enters: carrier `c` is an approach to intersection `x`. -/
def enters (c x : Arg) : Formula := .atom "st_lane_enters" [c, x] []

/-- st.lane_direction component of a carrier (normalised as Core reads it). -/
def dirComp (c : Arg) (k : String) : Term := .measure "st_lane_direction" [c, .lit k]

/-- f: the designated directions of c1 and c2 are opposed: their dot product is below −p.oncoming_heading_cos. -/
def opposedCarriers : Formula :=
  .cmp (.add (.mul (dirComp vC1 "x") (dirComp vC2 "x")) (.mul (dirComp vC1 "y") (dirComp vC2 "y")))
    .lt (.neg pOncomingHeadingCos)

/-- e, h: danger of a crash / immediate hazard — the centres of subject and v approach within
    p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance. -/
def conflict : Formula :=
  .and (.derived "prim_closest_approach_within" [vSubject, vV] [pConflictHorizon])
       (.cmp (.quantity "prim_closest_approach_distance" [vSubject, vV] [pConflictHorizon]) .lt pConflictCentreClearance)

/-- e: the subject proceeds — kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance. -/
def proceeds : Formula := .cmp (.measure "kin_speed" [vSubject]) .gt pHaltSpeedTolerance

/-- b, c: the subject's footprint overlaps intersection X and it declares int.left_turn at X. -/
def selectsX : Formula :=
  .and (occupies vSubject vX) (.intent "int.left_turn" vSubject vX)

/-- c1: a carrier (not X itself) entering X that the subject occupied when it last entered X:
    it has overlapped X continuously since an observation at which it occupied c1. -/
def entryCarrier : Formula :=
  .and (.not (.same vC1 vX))
    (.and (enters vC1 vX) (.since (occupies vSubject vX) (occupies vSubject vC1)))

/-- f, g, h: v is another vehicle approaching from the opposite direction — on a carrier c2 (not X
    itself) entering X, or in X continuously since it occupied such a c2, c2's direction opposed to
    c1's — and v either overlaps X or, on c2, is in conflict with the subject. -/
def opposingVehicle : Formula :=
  .and (isVehicle vV)
    (.and (.not (.same vV vSubject))
      (.existsRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c2"
        (.and (.not (.same vC2 vX))
          (.and (enters vC2 vX)
            (.and (.since (occupies vV vX) (occupies vV vC2))
              (.and opposedCarriers
                (.or (occupies vV vX) (.and (occupies vV vC2) conflict))))))))

/-- d, e: yield — no contact with v, and not proceeding while in conflict with v. -/
def yields : Formula :=
  .and (.not (.atom "rel_contact" [vSubject, vV] []))
       (.not (.and proceeds conflict))

/-- Class of `subject`: ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle -/
def clsSubject : Formula := isVehicle vSubject

/-- Applicability: b (trigger): within an intersection; c (trigger): intending to turn to the left.
    The conditions f, g select the protected vehicles inside the obligation, as the record states. -/
def applicability : Formula := .existsRegion (.lit "intersection") "X" selectsX

/-- Obligation: d (obligation): shall yield; e (standard): the right-of-way; h (standard): or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard -/
def obligation : Formula :=
  .forallRegion (.lit "intersection") "X"
    (.implies selectsX
      (.forallRegion (.lit "travel_region") "c1"
        (.implies entryCarrier
          (.forallUser "v" (.implies opposingVehicle yields)))))

def rule : Rule :=

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
3	  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
4	  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.
5	
6	  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
7	  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
8	  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.
9	
10	  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
11	  writes through a `Units` constructor.
12	-/
13	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
14	
15	namespace TrafficSpec
16	namespace Build
17	
18	/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
19	def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
20	def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
21	def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
22	def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))
23	
24	def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)
25	
26	/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
27	    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
28	def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
29	    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
30	  { track := track
31	    classes := some classes
32	    kin := { position := some pos
33	             heading := some heading
34	             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
35	             speed := some speed
36	             extent := some halfExtent
37	             pathLength := pathLength } }
38	
39	/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
40	def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
41	  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }
42	
43	def withSignals (u : RoadUser) (f : Signals → Signals) : RoadUser := { u with sig := f u.sig }
44	def withKin (u : RoadUser) (f : Kin → Kin) : RoadUser := { u with kin := f u.kin }
45	/-- A measured relation from `a` to `b`, with the measured fields the source supplies. -/
46	def relation (a b : TrackId) (f : MeasuredRelation → MeasuredRelation := id) : MeasuredRelation := f { a := a, b := b }
47	def withRelations (s : Scene) (rs : List MeasuredRelation) : Scene := { s with relations := rs }
48	
49	/-- A region of a kind with a polygon boundary. -/
50	def region (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (boundary : List Vec) : Structure :=
51	  { id := id, kind := kind, boundary := some boundary }
52	/-- An axis-aligned rectangular region from two corners. -/
53	def rect (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
54	  region id kind [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]
55	/-- A lane with its direction and neighbours. -/
56	def lane (id : RegionId) (boundary : List Vec) (direction : Vec)
57	    (left right : Option RegionId := none) (ordinal count : Option Nat := none)
58	    (leadsTo : Option (List RegionId) := none) (enters : Option RegionId := none) : Structure :=
59	  { id := id
60	    kind := .lane
61	    boundary := some boundary
62	    lane := some { direction := some direction, leftNeighbour := left, rightNeighbour := right,
63	                   ordinalFromLeft := ordinal, countInDirection := count, leadsTo := leadsTo,
64	                   entersIntersection := enters } }
65	def point (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (pos : Vec) : Structure :=
66	  { id := id, kind := kind, position := some pos }
67	
68	def device (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) (pos : Option Vec := none) : Device :=
69	  { id := id, kind := kind, governs := governs, position := pos }
70	def signal (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (shows : List SignalIndication) : Device :=
71	  { device id .trafficSignal governs with indications := some shows }
72	def sign (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) : Device := device id kind governs
73	def speedLimit (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (value : Q) (kind : SpeedSignKind) : Device :=
74	  { device id .speedLimitSign governs with speedValue := some value, speedKind := some kind }
75	def zoneSign (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (kind : ZoneKind) (isEnd : Bool)
76	    (conditions : Option Conditions := none) : Device :=
77	  { device id .zoneSign governs with zoneKind := some kind, isEnd := some isEnd, conditions := conditions }
78	
79	/-- Occupancy from the geometry: every user inside every region whose boundary contains its position. -/
80	def occupancyFromGeometry (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
81	  users.flatMap fun u =>
82	    match u.kin.position with
83	    | none => []
84	    | some p => structures.filterMap fun st =>
85	      match st.boundary with
86	      | some poly => if Geom.inPolygon p poly then some (u.track, st.id) else none
87	      | none => none
88	
89	/-- A scene; occupancy is derived from geometry unless given. -/
90	def scene (t : Timestamp) (subject : Option TrackId) (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure)
91	    (devices : List Device) (occupies : Option (List (TrackId × RegionId)) := none)
92	    (env : Env := {}) (assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
93	  { t := t
94	    subject := subject
95	    users := users
96	    structures := structures
97	    devices := devices
98	    occupancyObserved := users.map (·.track)
99	    occupies := occupies.getD (occupancyFromGeometry users structures)
100	    env := env
101	    assumptions := assumptions
102	    intents := intents }
103	
104	/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
105	def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
106	  (List.range n).map fun k =>
107	    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
108	      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
109	    f k t
110	
111	/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
112	    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
113	def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
114	  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
115	  | some first, some last =>
116	    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
117	    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
118	    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
119	    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
120	    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }

/-

  Geometry (every figure the witness's own, none in the rule): intersection X = region 10, the
  square x, y ∈ [−10, 10] m. Three approach lanes enter it:

    12 (c2)  the opposing approach from the north, x ∈ [−4, 0], y ∈ [10, 60], direction south;
    13       a cross-street approach from the east, x ∈ [10, 60], y ∈ [0, 4], direction west.
  Bodies are cars of half-length 2 m, half-width 1 m. Instants are 1 s apart; occupancy is stated
  per scene. The subject (track 1) declares int.left_turn at X (true, or false in `idle`).
  At k = 0 the subject is on lane 11 only (not in X), so every `since` look-back is decided there.
  Conflict figures (reading: horizon 3 s, centre clearance 3 m, halt tolerance 0.1 m/s):
    forbid/blind k=1: subject (2, 2) westbound 2 m/s, v (−2, 13) southbound 5 m/s on lane 12:
      closest approach at 63/29 ≈ 2.17 s, centre distance ≈ 0.37 m.
    branch_3 k=1: v (−2, 7) inside X: closest approach ≈ 1.14 s at ≈ 1.85 m.

import TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders

def m (n : Int) : Q := Units.metres n

/-- c1: the subject's approach from the south, northbound, entering X. -/

  Build.lane 11 [(m 0, m (-60)), (m 4, m (-60)), (m 4, m (-10)), (m 0, m (-10))] Build.north (enters := some 10)
/-- c2: the opposing approach from the north, southbound, entering X. -/

/-- A cross-street approach from the east, westbound, entering X. -/

  Build.lane 13 [(m 10, m 0), (m 60, m 0), (m 60, m 4), (m 10, m 4)] Build.west (enters := some 10)

def roadMap : List Structure := [intersection, southApproach, northApproach, eastApproach]

/-- A car at (x, y) m with a heading and a speed in m/s. -/

# NRS_484B_253_o1 — task result

## Final verdict: OK

(7 witnesses, 10 names, composes nothing)

## Gate runs

1. **UNUSED_CLAIM** — this run was on the harness skeleton, before any edits, so every claimed name was still unused. I ran it to see a baseline; strictly it wasn't needed. Earlier, I also tried a malformed command (the gate command with `--help` piped to `head`). The sandbox denied it and it did not run.
2. **OK** — after writing the rule and the seven witnesses described below.

## How the rule is written

- **Class (a):** `ru_aggregate subject "DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"`.
- **Applicability (b, c):** there is an intersection X (quantifier kind `intersection`) that the subject occupies (`rel_occupies`), with `intent int.left_turn subject X` read at the judged observation.
- **Obligation:**
  - **X:** re-bound with the same selection as the applicability, for every such X.
  - **c1:** every `travel_region` c1 for which `st_lane_enters c1 X` holds and `since (occupies subject X) (occupies subject c1)` holds (the subject has been in X continuously since it occupied c1).
  - **v:** every road user v that is a vehicle (aggregate), is not the subject, and has some `travel_region` c2 where:
    - `st_lane_enters c2 X` holds;
    - `since (occupies v X) (occupies v c2)` holds;
    - the dot product of the `st_lane_direction` vectors of c1 and c2 is below `−p.oncoming_heading_cos`;
    - and either v occupies X (g), or v occupies c2 and is in conflict (h). Conflict means `prim_closest_approach_within` at `p.conflict_horizon` and `prim_closest_approach_distance` below `p.conflict_centre_clearance`.
  - **Duty (d, e):** the subject is not in contact with v (`rel_contact`), and it is not the case that it proceeds (`kin_speed > p.halt_speed_tolerance`) while in that conflict.

## Choices the node left open

- **X excluded as a carrier (structural, not a narrowing):** c1 and c2 range over travel regions, and X is itself one. Core reads `st_lane_enters` on a region with no lane information as *unknown*, so X as a candidate carrier would leave compliant verdicts unknown. X is not a carrier that enters itself, so I added `not (same c1 X)` and `not (same c2 X)`. The header comment records this.
- **"Occupies c2 now" is covered by `since`:** the record says v "occupies a carrier c2 entering X, or overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied such a c2". `since` already covers the first case, so a separate first disjunct would have been redundant.
- No narrowings were declared.

## Witnesses

- **`forbid`:** violated, with v on lane 12 and outside X.
- **`permit`:** compliant; the subject waits at rest while v crosses X, then turns.
- **`idle`:** not applicable, because the intent is declared false.
- **`blind`:** unknown, from the `forbid` trace with `kin.speed` masked.
- **`branch_1`:** compliant, with no other user in the scene.
- **`branch_2`:** compliant; v comes from the cross street on lane 13, whose direction is perpendicular to c1's.
- **`branch_3` (added):** violated, with v inside X and no longer on c2. This exercises the "within the intersection" limb (g).

## Why I finished

The gate returned OK.

The gate returned **OK** for NRS_484B_253_o1 (7 witnesses), using 2 of the 6 runs.

**What the rule says:**
- **Who and when:** the subject must be a vehicle under DEF-NRS-484A-320, and the rule applies when it is in an intersection X and has `int.left_turn` declared at X.
- **The vehicles it must yield to:**
  - c1 is the approach lane the subject came in on.
  - v is any other vehicle that came in on (or is still on) an approach c2 whose direction is roughly opposite c1's: the dot product is below −`p.oncoming_heading_cos`.
  - v counts if it is inside X, or if it is still on c2 and in conflict with the subject. "In conflict" means their centres come within `p.conflict_centre_clearance` within `p.conflict_horizon`.
- **The duty:** the subject must not touch v, and must not move faster than `p.halt_speed_tolerance` while in that conflict.

**One choice the node didn't spell out:** the lane quantifiers also pick up the intersection itself, because it counts as a travel region. Core treats "does this lane enter X" as unknown for a region that isn't a lane, which would have turned the compliant witnesses into unknown. An intersection can't be an approach into itself, so I excluded X from both lane positions (`not (same c1 X)`, `not (same c2 X)`). I recorded this in the rule's header comment as a structural choice, not a narrowing, and declared no narrowings.

**Witnesses:** the six planned ones (`forbid`, `permit`, `idle`, `blind`, `branch_1`, `branch_2`) plus one I added. `branch_3` is a violation where the oncoming car is already inside the intersection and off its lane. It is the only witness that exercises the "within the intersection" case.

**Two things outside the plan:**
- My first gate run was on the untouched skeleton, which returned UNUSED_CLAIM. That run wasn't needed and used up one of the six.
- Before that, I mistakenly tried the gate command with extra arguments (`--help` piped to `head`). The sandbox denied it and it never ran.

The full account is in `task_result.md` in the working directory.
